title: siem-integration-customer-requirements-and-adapter-patterns
body:
Purpose
This doc captures pragmatic customer-facing requirements, adapter design patterns, and connector-spec guidance for SIEM exports (Splunk, Datadog, Microsoft Sentinel). It ties together RBAC v2 considerations, the audit-log schema we emit, and evidence-automation hooks so integrations are reliable, testable, and compliant.

Scope
- Target integrations: Splunk (HEC), Datadog Logs API, Azure/Microsoft Sentinel (Log Analytics / Event Hub ingestion).
- Deliverables: onboarding checklist, acceptance criteria, field-mapping examples, connector error modes, transformation guidance, and sample payloads.
- Not in scope: customer-side SIEM ingestion tuning, internal billing metrics.

High-level requirements (customer-facing)
1) Minimal setup: Customer supplies endpoint (HEC URL / Datadog EU/US API URL / Azure Event Hub connection string) and an auth secret. Support Opaque API keys and mTLS where available.
2) Configurable export modes: streaming (near-real-time) and daily batch (for lower maturity customers).
3) RBAC awareness: exports must respect RBAC v2 scope — only events the requesting service account can read are exported.
4) PII handling: customers can opt into automatic redaction rules (email/hash, credit-card redaction, full-field drop).
5) Evidence bundles: for compliance customers, connector must be able to attach or reference an evidence bundle for an audit window (signed link or S3 presigned url).
6) Delivery guarantees: at-least-once with deduplication idempotency tokens; configurable retry/backoff policy.

RBAC v2 considerations
- Mapping: map internal RBAC roles -> SIEM export scopes. Example mapping: organization.admin -> full-audit (all org-level events); team.readonly -> team-scoped events only.
- Scoped tokens: connectors should accept a short-lived export token that embeds RBAC scope (JWT with aud=siem-export). Server validates token before streaming events.
- Audit of export requests: every export request must itself generate an audit event (export.requested, export.approved/denied) with requester identity and scope.

Audit log schema (reference)
We emit a canonical event envelope. Below is a flattened plaintext example (field names must be preserved):
- event_id: uuid-v4
- timestamp: ISO-8601
- event_type: string (e.g., auth.login, model.infer, config.change)
- actor: { id, type, email } encoded as actor_id, actor_type, actor_email
- resource: { id, type, name } encoded as resource_id, resource_type, resource_name
- action: string (create/read/update/delete/trigger)
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- reason: free text for failure (optional)
- request_id: correlation id (from serving runtime)
- sequence_index: incremental integer (per request/session)
- rbac_scope: textual representation (org:123/team:456/role:viewer)
- pii_masking: schema version used
- evidence_ref: optional url or s3-ref for bundles
- raw_payload: base64 JSON (optional, controlled by customer)
- metadata: free-form tags (comma-separated)

Field mapping guidance for SIEMs
- Splunk (HEC): map event envelope to a single HEC event with fields:event_id, event_type, actor_email, resource_type, outcome, request_id, and put raw_payload into _raw if enabled. Use index and sourceType configurable per customer.
- Datadog: send as logs API v2 JSON; include "ddsource"="redwood-inference" and set "service"="redwood-audit". Use attributes for rbac_scope and evidence_ref.
- Sentinel (Log Analytics): send as JSON to a custom log type (RedwoodAudit_CL). Flatten nested fields using _ and append _t for text fields (e.g., actor_email_t).

Connector patterns and adapters
1) Transport abstraction: have a small adapter layer per SIEM that implements: auth(), sendBatch(events[]), healthCheck(). This keeps retry logic and batching uniform.
2) Batching policy: default 1s or 5s flush for streaming; size-limited batch (max 500 events or 5MB). Customers can tune to match throughput.
3) Backpressure: if SIEM returns 429 or 5xx, exponential backoff with jitter, and escalate to support after N failures (configurable).
4) Idempotency: include event_id and request_id; when sending batch, include deduplication keys where supported (e.g., Splunk has event.metadata).
5) Transform rules: allow per-customer JSONPath mapping with built-in safe transformations (hash-PII, drop-field, truncate). Keep transform config versioned.

Auth and security
- Splunk: support HEC token + optional mTLS cert validation. HEC token rotated via UI/CLI. Token must be stored in KMS.
- Datadog: API key in header (DD-API-KEY) and ability to use proxy for private VPC setups.
- Azure Sentinel: prefer Event Hub with SAS key or Managed Identity when using Azure resources.
- E2E TLS required. Support validating customer cert subject for mutual TLS.

Evidence automation hooks
- Bundle creation: for requested audit windows, platform packages evidence (logs, config snapshots, model hashes) into signed tar.gz with manifest.json and content-hash.
- Delivery: connector includes evidence_ref in events and can optionally POST evidence to customer-specified S3/HTTP endpoint using presigned URL.
- Retention policy: configurable per customer; default 90 days. Evidence access must be logged and produce additional audit events.

Operational acceptance criteria (customer onboarding)
- Smoke test: send 10 synthetic events, verify arrival in customer SIEM within agreed latency SLA (streaming <= 30s typical).
- RBAC test: request export token scoped to team X and verify only team X events exported.
- PII test: enable redaction profile and verify no PII fields in events.
- Evidence test: request evidence bundle for 7-day window and verify file integrity (manifest hash matches).
- Failure mode test: simulate SIEM 5xx and verify exponential backoff and alert generation.

Monitoring and SLOs
- Latency p50/p95 measured from event generation to delivery. Target p95 < 60s for streaming.
- Delivery success rate per tenant > 99.5% monthly.
- Connector health: per-customer error-rate, last-successful-heartbeat, queued-events. Expose via Redwood Console dashboards.

Common error modes and remediation
- 401/403: token misconfiguration or RBAC scope mismatch. Remediation: validate export token scope and renew.
- 429: rate limit - apply backoff and request customer SIEM rate increase if persistent.
- 413 payload too large: reduce batch size or truncate raw_payload.
- 500+/gateway errors: transient; backoff; escalate to SRE if > N minutes.

Onboarding matrix (quick reference)
- Bronze (low maturity): daily batch CSV export -> customer SFTP. Minimal RBAC enforcement (org-level only).
- Silver: streaming to Datadog/Splunk with basic redaction. Scoped tokens supported.
- Gold (enterprise): mTLS + Event Hub ingestion for Sentinel, evidence automation, full RBAC v2 enforcement, retention/archival policies, SLA.

Sample payloads (flattened)
1) Splunk HEC event (single line JSON as HEC event):
{
  "time": "2026-03-09T18:12:34Z",
  "host": "redwood-inference",
  "source":"redwood:audit",
  "event": {"event_id":"e9f1...","event_type":"config.change","actor_email":"alice@acme.com","resource_type":"deployment","outcome":"success","request_id":"r-123"},
  "fields": {"rbac_scope":"org:55/team:24/role:admin","evidence_ref":"s3://redwood-evidence/123.tar.gz"}
}

2) Datadog log snippet:
{
  "message":"config.change by alice@acme.com",
  "ddsource":"redwood-inference",
  "service":"redwood-audit",
  "attributes": {"event_id":"e9f1...","rbac_scope":"org:55/team:24"},
  "timestamp": 1700000000
}

Documentation & support artifacts to deliver
- Connector quickstart (1-pager) per SIEM with exact curl examples and sample config.
- Field-mapping reference (CSV) with canonical schema -> Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel columns.
- Onboarding checklist (for solutions engineering) with acceptance criteria.
- Incident runbook for connector failures.

Next steps
- Review with Solutions Engineering & SRE for rate-limit knobs and default batch sizing.
- Draft quickstart pages and sample curl commands for Splunk HEV, Datadog Logs API, Azure Event Hub.
- Implement export-request audit events in serving runtime and wire evidence bundle generation into connector flow.

Unresolved questions (notes)
- Do customers want per-tenant deduplication TTLs? (tradeoffs: memory vs risk of duplicate events)
- Should evidence bundles be signed with customer-specific keys or Redwood managed keys?

Notes to self
- Coordinate with Lina on the RBAC token claim format.
- Add acceptance-tests to github/siem-adapters e2e suite.
